title: Enhancing Cross-Document Event Coreference Resolution by Discourse Structure and Semantic Information
research_question: Can document-level discourse structure and cross-document semantic information improve the identification and clustering of mentions that refer to the same event across documents?
methodology: The authors propose DIE-EC, which combines contextual mention representations with document-level Rhetorical Structure Theory trees and cross-document lexical chains in heterogeneous graphs processed by graph attention networks. A pairwise scorer estimates whether event mentions corefer, after which agglomerative clustering creates event clusters. The paper also constructs WEC-Zh from Chinese Wikipedia links, yielding 53,066 event mentions in 4,476 clusters, with manually cross-validated development and test subsets. Experiments on WEC-Zh, WEC-Eng, and ECB+ use standard event-coreference metrics and include component ablations and analyses by lexical overlap and document length.

key_findings.finding: Combining discourse structure and lexical-chain semantics improves cross-document event-coreference performance over the evaluated baselines on both English and Chinese datasets.
On WEC-Zh, DIE-EC reports a CoNLL F1 of 66.9 compared with 62.1 for the cited WEC baseline, with improvements also reported for B3 and CEAF metrics.

Ablation experiments show that removing lexical chains causes a larger performance reduction than removing RST structure, indicating that cross-document semantic coherence contributes strongly to event identity decisions.

Lexical chains are especially useful when event mentions have little direct lexical overlap, with substantially larger F1 degradation when the lexical-chain component is removed in the low-overlap subset.
RST-based discourse information becomes more useful for long documents, where removing the RST component produces larger performance losses.

The model can distinguish highly similar but non-coreferential event mentions when contextual lexical chains expose differences such as time or location, supporting the importance of concrete event arguments for identity.

The study does not model partial, subevent, overlapping, or non-transitive continuity as separate relation types; binary pairwise coreference decisions are ultimately converted into disjoint event clusters.

The datasets are Wikipedia- and benchmark-derived rather than enterprise email, chat, or organizational workflow communications, so transfer to longitudinal work-item linking is not empirically established.

limitations: WEC-Zh derives much of its supervision from Wikipedia hyperlink structure, which is only a proxy for independently adjudicated real-world event identity.
Manual cross-validation is concentrated in development and test construction rather than providing fully manual annotation of the complete training corpus.
Reported Fleiss' kappa of 0.71 indicates substantial but not perfect annotator agreement.
Performance depends on upstream discourse parsing and lexical-chain construction quality.
Agglomerative clustering produces equivalence-like event groups and does not represent asymmetric, partial, overlapping, subevent, or non-transitive continuity relations.
The work does not evaluate enterprise email, chat, ticketing, or other organizational workflow streams.
The evaluation is primarily static cross-document coreference rather than longitudinal identity maintenance as work items evolve over time.
raw_claims: DIE-EC augments event mentions with both document-level discourse relations and cross-document semantic links.
RST structures and lexical chains are converted into heterogeneous graphs and encoded with graph attention networks.
Pairwise event-coreference scores are followed by agglomerative clustering to create event groups.
WEC-Zh contains 53,066 event mentions organized into 4,476 clusters.
The Chinese dataset is derived from Wikipedia anchors that refer to the same underlying subject and is cleaned for event mentions.
The development and test data were checked by two annotators, with reported Fleiss' kappa of 0.71.
The complete model outperforms the compared WEC baseline on the reported WEC-Zh aggregate metrics.
Removing lexical chains hurts performance more than removing discourse structure in the reported ablations.
Lexical-chain information is particularly valuable when mentions share little surface vocabulary.
Discourse structure contributes more strongly when documents become long.
Time and location information can help separate superficially similar mentions that actually denote different events.
The final representation of identity is a cluster of coreferential mentions rather than a graded or overlapping continuity relation.
